entry.title: AI inference is becoming a memory engineering problem
entry.summary: The most technical AI story right now is not a new model. It is the brutal physics of inference. Once you move past the prefill step, decoding is dominated by memory traffic. Every generated token pulls attention state back into the GPU, and that state keeps growing with context length. The industry name for that state is the KV cache, and it is quietly turning AI into a memory hierarchy design problem. The key shift is that teams are starting to treat context like a reusable asset, not a temporary byproduct. If you can retrieve multi gigabyte inference state in milliseconds instead of regenerating it in seconds, you change accelerator utilization and you change cost.
